Title: Sort polygons
Learning intention: I am learning to sort polygons by number of sides, concavity and regularity
Teaching support: A polygon is concave if one interior angle is greater than 180° (an inward dent); otherwise it is convex. A convex polygon is regular only if all sides and all angles are equal. Name it by its number of sides.
Worked example: Type the group for polygon A: the sorter's output and its name, for example Regular pentagon. Answer: Concave pentagon. Shape A answers Yes to “Any interior angle greater than 180°?”, so it reaches Concave. It has 5 sides, so it is a concave pentagon.
Reasoning example: How many of these six polygons are hexagons? Answer: 3. B, C, F.
Application example: Sort each polygon into its group: the sorter's output, then its name from its number of sides. Answer: Concave pentagon|Regular hexagon|Irregular hexagon|Irregular pentagon|Regular pentagon|Concave hexagon. A: Concave pentagon. B: Regular hexagon. C: Irregular hexagon. D: Irregular pentagon. E: Regular pentagon. F: Concave hexagon.

Title: Fix a broken sorter
Learning intention: I am learning to find the shapes a sorter puts in the wrong group and fix it
Teaching support: Run every test shape through the sorter and compare its group with the correct one. A shape in the wrong group shows which question or branch to change.
Worked example: Run each polygon through this sorter. One lands in the wrong group. Type its letter. Answer: C. Shape C answers No to “Any interior angle greater than 180°?” and Yes to “Exactly 5 sides?”, so it reaches Regular convex. But shape C is irregular convex, so the sorter puts it in the wrong group.
Reasoning example: Run each polygon through this sorter. How many land in the wrong group? Answer: 1. C land in the wrong group.
Application example: This polygon sorter puts some shapes in the wrong group. Change boxes so every test shape reaches its group. Run it, then check. Answer: concave|Concave|regular|Regular convex|Irregular convex. One sorter that works: ask “Any interior angle greater than 180°?” (Yes → Concave), then “All sides and all angles equal?” (Yes → Regular convex, No → Irregular convex). Run every shape again after each change.

Title: Design your own sorter
Learning intention: I am learning to design a complete sorter for a set of shapes and justify it
Teaching support: List the groups you need. A yes/no sorter needs one question fewer than the number of groups. Choose questions that use defining properties, then test every shape.
Worked example: A sorter must separate 6 groups using yes/no questions. How many questions does it need? Answer: 5. Each yes/no question splits one branch into two, adding one group. Starting from 1 group, 6 groups need 6 − 1 = 5 questions.
Reasoning example: Both sorters use the same two questions in opposite orders. Type the group both give for quadrilateral A. Answer: Non-square rhombus. Shape A answers No to “Four right angles?” and Yes to “Four equal sides?”, so it reaches Non-square rhombus. Both questions are asked on every route, so the order does not change the group.
Application example: Design a polygon sorter: choose a question or group for every box so each test shape reaches its group. Run it, then check. Answer: concave|Concave|regular|Regular convex|Irregular convex. One sorter that works: ask “Any interior angle greater than 180°?” (Yes → Concave), then “All sides and all angles equal?” (Yes → Regular convex, No → Irregular convex).
